description: Structural template of every Vitae '+ New' entity (NODE_TYPES) and how entities may relate via EDGE_TYPES. Hand-maintained mirror of packages/core schemas and form descriptors (synced 2026-07-29), not a runtime import format (see vitae.graph.bundle/1 for that).

field_notation.type: JSON-ish type: string | number | boolean | object | array | date (YYYY-MM-DD) | datetime (ISO-8601) | email | url | record
field_notation.required: true only when Zod (or form) requires the field on create
field_notation.enum: closed set of allowed string/number values

node_envelope.description: Shared fields on every node. Per-type data lives in props.

edge_envelope.description: Shared fields on every relationship. Direction is src → dst.

is_placeholder.note: Reserved owner for records with no subject edge.

person.notes: Manual create may auto-add KNOWS from self. Add Connection also covers typed KNOWS (relation), STUDIED_AT, FOUNDED, and REPORTS_TO beyond form_edges.

organization.notes: Create form has no inline edges; Add Connection exposes ORG_RELATED (parent, partner, competitor, ...) and other legal org endpoints.

skills_gained.note: free-text mirror; real links are USES_SKILL edges

form_edges.note: For a comment, point at the parent post

github_id.note: Numeric GitHub repository id, stored for merge. Identity is github:repo:<id>, not this field alone.

loc_ref.note: e.g. p. 141 or 32:10 within the source

interviewers.note: free-text mirror; real interviewers are WITH → person

interaction.notes: Also has specialized POST /v1/interactions for one-tap logging.

project_id.note: Workspace node id of the project this task belongs to, when known.

location.notes: Typically a dst of LOCATED_IN / VISITED rather than an edge source.

relations.description: Canonical EDGE_TYPES with allowed src→dst endpoints (edgeEndpointsAllowed). '*' means any node type. PART_OF uses an explicit pair allow-list. PERSON_RELATIONS / ORG_RELATION_KINDS are enums for KNOWS.relation and ORG_RELATED.kind.

KNOWS.label: Knows

relation.note: Self's view of the other person; optional for backward compatibility

KNOWS.notes: Person ↔ person, typed relationship (friend, colleague, family, ...).

ATTENDED.label: Attended
ATTENDED.notes: For school/programs prefer STUDIED_AT; ATTENDED still allows education.

RELATES_TO.label: Relates to
RELATES_TO.notes: Typed catch-all between any two records

STUDIED_AT.label: Studied at
STUDIED_AT.notes: Person → school/organization or education program as a student.

REPORTS_TO.label: Reports to
REPORTS_TO.notes: Directed org-chart link; not the same as KNOWS.

ORG_RELATED.label: Related org
ORG_RELATED.notes: Src is the org in hand (e.g. Acme → parent → HoldingCo).

INTRODUCED.label: Introduced

via.note: The credited broker; a person id when recorded from a profile

INTRODUCED.notes: The two people connected by an introduction (FR-COMM-003); the warm-path search reads it as a hop.

DEPENDS_ON.label: Depends on
DEPENDS_ON.notes: Task → task that must finish first. Cycle detection is a pure check, not a DB constraint.

SERVES_GOAL.label: Serves goal
SERVES_GOAL.notes: Task or project → the goal it serves.

WAITING_ON.label: Waiting on
WAITING_ON.notes: Task → the person or organization it is blocked on.

FOR.label: For
FOR.notes: Task → the person, organization, or application it is for.

example_graph.description: Minimal populated slice showing career wiring, typed KNOWS.relation, and ORG_RELATED. Use bundle-local refs the same way as vitae.graph.bundle/1.
